Q: How can I unpack packed-refs? A:

The reason the packed refs exist is to speed up access in a repository with zillions of refs. It's easier to look at a single file with many lines than to hit the file system once for every single ref. Anything in Git (version control) which needs to know about refs goes through code which can read both the refs directory and the packed refs file. Unpacking it would defeat its purpose. If you want to access refs, use the plumbing commands (e.g., show-ref, for-each-ref, update-ref, etc.). I can't really think of any kind of access which would be faster and easier with the directory structure than with the plumbing commands (especially with for-each-ref available).

And yes, packed objects are (like packed refs) created for improved performance, but there's a huge difference. A packed refs file is just a bunch of independent lines. You can, essentially for free, add to or remove from it. There's no need to unpack it in order to modify it. Packed objects, on the other hand, are delta-compressed, so the objects inside depend on each other. They greatly reduce disk usage, and objects can be read from them at reasonable cost, but attempting to modify the set of objects in the pack is much more expensive than modifying loose objects, so it's only done periodically by git repack (called by git gc), though I don't believe git repack actually unpacks the objects - it just reads them from the packfile, packs them with the loose ones, and makes a new pack.

However, when a pack is transferred from a remote, it's unpacked on the local side. I see a call to an unpack method in the git receive-pack source, and the pack-objects manpage says:

The git unpack-objects command can read the packed archive and expand the objects contained in the pack into "one-file one-object" format; this is typically done by the smart-pull commands when a pack is created on-the-fly for efficient network transport by their peers.

Q: Logging all connections using iptables to closed ports A:

iptables has a socket module that can be used to determine if there is a listening socket matching an inbound packet.

iptables -N port-unreachable
iptables -A port-unreachable -m socket --nowildcard -j RETURN
iptables -A port-unreachable -j LOG --log-level info --log-prefix 'port unreachable: '

Likewise, the inverse:

iptables -N port-reachable
iptables -A port-reachable -m socket --nowildcard -j LOG --log-level info --log-prefix 'port reachable: '

Then you can add one or both rules to your INPUT chain:

iptables -I INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j port-unreachable
iptables -I INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j port-reachable

Additional matches can be used to further filter traffic before logging.

Q: Why is casting to object first needed to satisfy the compiler but the compiler also says casting to object was unnecessary A:

You can't cast a List<string?> to a List<string> or vice versa, because the underlying type is the same. Nullability works on the basis of compiler inference, not casting so casting is not relevant here. You need to just assign the value in a way that the compiler understands that it it's non-null in the first place. And the compiler does not understand the implication of if (xs.Exists(x => x is null)) as that's nested deep within the List code.

So you've started off with a List<string?>. Now you cannot get the compiler to assume this is a List<string> because that would then allow you to pass it to other code which only wants a List<string>, which the compiler cannot guarantee: as far as it can see, anything could be going on inside the List which might allow it to return a null.

If you are confident that your List<string> actually contains no nulls and is therefore safe to assume non-nullability, then use the ! postfix operator to tell the compiler to shut up.

List<string> ys = xs!;

But I would recommend you make the xs list non-nullable to start with.

Q: Launch PyCharm Environment from Anaconda Navigator A:

Adding the directory path of Pycharm to the configuration of Anaconda Navigator may solve the problem.

Open the Anaconda Navigator, click "File" - "Preferences", add the directory path of Pycharm in the "Pycharm Pro path" or "Pycharm CE path", depending on your Pycharm type. The directory path here should be the whole directory, for example, "C:\Pycharm".

Wish it helps!
